title: Business Development Manager, DACH
salary_basis: Based on senior role compensation records at Siteminder
description_html:
At SiteMinder, we believe our success comes from our people. We build diverse, inclusive teams where different voices, backgrounds and perspectives are valued. Our differences drive innovation for our customers, and our people bring the ideas, expertise and energy that help us keep moving forward. We’re better together.

What we do...

Right now, somewhere in the world, a hotel is taking a booking or increasing their revenue through technology you could help build. SiteMinder is the world’s leading hotel commerce platform. For more than 20 years, we’ve helped hotels attract guests, maximise revenue, forecast demand and perform at their best. Today, our platform supports 56,000+ hotels in 150+ countries, connects to 3,000+ partners and powers more than 140m reservations and AU$85 billion+ in hotel revenue each year.

That’s the kind of impact your work can have here. You’ll solve meaningful challenges with AI, simplify complexity and build solutions that help hotels perform. Supported by clear purpose, a strong platform and teams who care about what they’re building, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of an industry that never stands still.

As a Business Development Manager you will be a key driver of new business growth across the DACH region, engaging and advising customers across various segments from small independent hotels and boutique properties to large hotel groups and travel tech partners. You will be joining and representing the leading AI technology platform redefining guest acquisition and hotel revenue management. You will be relied on not just to close new business but to strategically influence pipeline growth, long-term partnerships and commercial excellence.

We won't throw you into the deep end - you'll be trained on our products, industry and sales processes. We have a month-long sales training and onboarding program to make sure you are set up for success. You will be supported by a dedicated sales coach and a buddy, as well as your team leader, who will coach, guide and motivate you to achieve your professional goals.

We know that an attractive compensation package is a key motivator in sales. SiteMinder offers you not only this, but also a working environment that represents ambition, collaboration, self-development and customer-centricity. If you identify with our core values (We Hustle, We Come Together, We Grow, We Make Things Simple) and you are a sales hunter at heart and able to work at a fast pace, we want to hear from you!

What You'll Do...

  • Lead full-cycle sales and business development: identify, engage and convert new prospects into customers.

  • Strategic territory and pipeline growth: define and execute strategic qualification routines, build segmented pipelines from your territory, and prioritise opportunities that deliver high value.

  • Consistently achieving sales KPIs and targets: work towards daily, weekly and monthly targets. Accountability will be important to help you succeed.

  • Trusted advisor engagement: conduct insightful discovery and product presentations, consulting on clients’ business and commercial goals, and present proposals to clients in a professional and confident manner. Negotiate contracts as required, maintaining a balance between optimal service and value for the client and SiteMinder's profit margins.

  • CRM ownership & intelligence: maintain disciplined CRM practices to ensure pipeline, forecasts, reporting, and customer insights are accurate and actionable.

  • Collaborate across functions: partner with Onboarding, Marketing, Product and Customer Success teams to refine market messaging, feedback loops, and go-to-market strategies that will improve our competitiveness.

  • Representing the company: work with local industry groups and travel associations to promote SiteMinder’s products and brand. Attend key functions and events, support webinars and other tactical initiatives to raise brand awareness, requiring occasional travel to client locations to attend meetings with relevant managers.

What You Have...

  • Sales & business development experience: extensive experience closing deals with full-cycle responsibility, ideally across SaaS, hospitality technology, hotel operations, revenue management, or related commercial services.

  • Industry fluency: solid understanding of the hospitality value chain (hotel management, revenue strategy, guest acquisition…).

  • Consultative and outcome-focused sales skills: demonstrated ability to diagnose business needs, tailor solutions and influence decision-making with impact.

  • Remote-ready communication & autonomy: excellent verbal and written communicator, strong listener, adept at building rapport and driving processes without day-to-day supervision.

  • Resilience & growth mindset: high level of self-motivation, curiosity to learn continuously and openness to feedback and coaching.

  • Analytical and tech-savvy: strong proficiency with CRM and sales tools.

  • Fluent in German (min. C2) and professional proficiency in English.

  • Please send us your CV in English!

Our Perks & Benefits…

  • Remote setup

  • Equity packages for you to share in SiteMinder's growth and successes

  • Investment in your personal growth

  • Uncapped commission that rewards overachievement

  • Excellence-driven, collaborative culture

  • Well-being initiatives

  • Referral bonus for bringing in new talent

  • Generous parental (including secondary) leave policy

  • Paid birthday, study and volunteering days off every year

  • Employee Resource Groups (ERG) to help you connect and get involved

Does this job sound like you? If yes, we'd love for you to be part of our team! Please send a copy of your resume and our Talent Acquisition team will be in touch.

When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any adjustments you may need during the interview process. We encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply.

Think this role sounds like you? If so, we’d love to hear from you. Please send us your resume and our Talent Acquisition team will be in touch.

 

When you apply, feel free to share your pronouns and let us know if you need any adjustments during the interview process, we’re here to support you. We also warmly encourage applications from people from underrepresented backgrounds.

title: Workplace and People Operations Manager
salary_basis: Based on senior role compensation records at Telli
description_html:
about us

Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.

For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.

AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to talk to their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.

At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of voice agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first voice agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI voice agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.

We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models. All of us like to challenge ourselves and take real ownership over what we do, all while still staying humble and keeping a low-ego culture.

Check out our principles to see how we work.

mission
As Workplace & People Operations Manager at telli, you own the environment our team does its best work in. You're responsible for keeping our Berlin office running smoothly day to day: workplace processes, people ops, internal events, and the culture initiatives that make telli feel like telli.

what you'll do:

  • run our Berlin office: supplies, equipment, and making sure we stay productive and well-organized

  • drive culture initiatives that keep the team connected as we grow

  • own the employee lifecycle, from onboarding (so new joiners have desk, hardware, and access ready before they walk in) to offboarding

  • build automations around workplace and people ops (ordering, inventory, requests) with AI and no-code tools

  • jump in wherever help is needed, because no two weeks look the same

what makes you a great fit:

  • you have a few years of experience in workplace, office, or people operations, ideally at a startup

  • you're hands-on and happy to do the unglamorous work that makes everything else possible

  • you're organized, reliable, and notice the details others miss

  • you build processes that scale instead of solving the same problem twice

  • you're curious about tools and automation and pick up new things fast

  • you take ownership and don't wait for detailed instructions

  • you communicate well in both English and German

  • you're a host at heart and love creating great experiences for others

you may not be a great fit if:

  • you only want to do high-level "strategic" work

  • juggling multiple things at once stresses you out

  • you want to work fully remote, since this role lives in the office

  • you'd rather watch than roll up your sleeves

title: Implementation Manager DACH
salary_basis: Based on senior role compensation records at Mollie
description_html:
Build with us

Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow – with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.

With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.

We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.

Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.

 

Your impact

As Implementation Manager, you'll own the post-sales integration phase for Mollie's largest and most complex deals, guiding merchants from handover through testing to go live. You'll run kickoffs with internal and external stakeholders, set go live dates, keep progress on track, and coordinate testing and feedback along the way. You'll work closely with colleagues across sales, product and engineering, as well as with merchants directly, keeping everyone aligned as deals move toward launch.

This function is newly formed, so you'll have real influence over how the role and its processes take shape, bringing in your own experience rather than following a fixed playbook. The role is also more technical than it might first appear: you'll get close to the real world edge cases and issues that surface once a solution meets implementation reality, giving you hands on technical exposure without needing a payments or engineering background going in.

Your work protects revenue by keeping live dates on track, and it supports how Mollie scales delivery more broadly, building a structured, dedicated integration phase for its biggest deals. You'll report to Jan-Jaap van Helden.

 

What you'll ship

  • Own the post sales integration phase for Mollie's largest and most complex deals, from handover through testing to go live

  • Run kickoffs with internal and external stakeholders, setting go live dates and keeping progress on track

  • Organise and track testing, raising issues and feedback as they surface

  • Coordinate across sales, product and engineering colleagues, as well as with merchants directly, to keep everyone aligned

  • Keep agreed go live dates on track, since delays mean missed revenue

  • Maintain documentation and playbooks that make delivery predictable and scalable

     

What you'll bring

  • Up to 3 years of experience in ecommerce or payments, in a similar role

  • Fluent in German and English, since this role supports the German market and works directly with local merchants

  • Strong organisational and structuring skills, with solid project management ability

  • Genuine technical interest and the ability to understand technical concepts such as APIs, since this role gets close to the edge cases that surface once a solution meets reality

  • An ownership mindset, taking charge of the implementation process rather than reacting to it, while staying flexible within agreed roles and processes

  • Honest, open communication style with a genuine, trustworthy manner, including a strong track record collaborating with pre-sales teams and handling conflict at handover

  • Payments or ecommerce experience, or familiarity with the ecosystem, is a strong plus though not required

 

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

 

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy

If you're excited by the idea of building what's next, for yourself and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV (in English) using the form below.

Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie is really like.

 

AI at Mollie

We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every team, every role, every day.

AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance with us.

title: Operativer Einkauf
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Sereact GmbH
description_html:
Wer wir sind:
Wir entwickeln die Intelligenz, die es Robotern ermöglicht, die reale Welt wahrzunehmen, zu verstehen und in ihr zu handeln – über das Labor hinaus und hinein in den industriellen Alltag, etwa in Lagerhallen und Fabriken. Unsere Technologie schließt die Automatisierungslücken, an denen klassische Systeme scheitern. Wir haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, die Art und Weise, wie körperliche Arbeit verrichtet wird, neu zu denken, und suchen neugierige, mutige Köpfe, die die Zukunft der Robotik gemeinsam mit uns gestalten wollen.


Überblick:
Wir suchen eine prozessorientierte Person, die im operativen technischen Einkauf, das kaufmännische Fundament unserer innovativen Robotiklösungen bei Sereact stärkt.
Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für unsere internen kaufmännischen Abläufe und bist ein echtes Organisationstalent, das sich gerne mitten ins Geschehen stürzt und dafür sorgt, dass unser Tagesgeschäft im Hintergrund reibungslos läuft.
Die Stelle ist in Stuttgart angesiedelt und eignet sich ideal für jemanden, der gerne strukturierte Prozesse aufbaut, kaufmännische Aufgaben steuert und ein Team unterstützt, das an modernster Technologie arbeitet.


Deine Aufgaben:

  • Projekt- und Auftragsmanagement: Du steuerst unsere Projekte aus kaufmännischer Sicht, von der ersten Bestellung bis zur finalen Lieferung.

  • Einkauf und Materialwirtschaft: Du unterstützt die Beschaffung von Komponenten und pflegst enge Beziehungen zu unseren Lieferanten.

  • Bestandsmanagement: Du behältst unsere Lagerbestände im Blick und stellst sicher, dass alle Komponenten zur richtigen Zeit am richtigen Ort sind.

  • Allgemeine Administration: Von der vorbereitenden Buchhaltung bis zur Stammdatenpflege sorgst du dafür, dass unser Tagesgeschäft reibungslos läuft.

Qualifikationen:

  • Ausbildung: Abgeschlossene Ausbildung zum Industriekaufmann/zur Industriekauffrau oder ein Studium der Betriebswirtschaftslehre.

  • Erfahrung: Mindestens 2 Jahre Berufserfahrung in einer kaufmännischen oder operativen Rolle.

  • Mindset: Du besitzt eine ausgeprägte Hands-on-Mentalität. Keine Aufgabe ist dir zu klein oder zu komplex, wenn das Team Unterstützung braucht.

  • Antrieb: Deine Motivation und Lernbereitschaft sind uns wichtiger als tiefgehendes Branchenwissen in der Robotik.

  • Kenntnisse: Sicherer Umgang mit MS Office, idealerweise Erfahrung mit ERP-Systemen. Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse sind erforderlich.

Unser Interviewprozess:

  • Bewerbung

  • Cultural-Fit-Interview (40 Min.): Ein Gespräch darüber, wie du arbeitest, was dich motiviert und wonach du suchst. Es erwarten dich Fragen zu deinem Lebenslauf, deinem „Warum" und Zeit für deine eigenen Fragen.

  • Fachliches Interview (45 Min.): Ein tieferer Einblick in deine Fähigkeiten und deinen Problemlösungsansatz für diese Rolle.

  • Gespräch mit den Gründern: Du triffst einen unserer Gründer, um über die Rolle und deinen Werdegang zu sprechen. Eine gute Gelegenheit, mehr über die Vision von Sereact zu erfahren, Fragen zu stellen und ein klares Gefühl für unsere Unternehmenskultur und Arbeitsumgebung zu bekommen.

Was wir bieten:

  • Wellpass (Fitnessstudio-Mitgliedschaft)

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten

  • Möglichkeit zum Homeoffice bei Bedarf

  • Ein motiviertes Team und eine offene Unternehmenskultur

  • Attraktive Vergütung und hervorragende Karrieremöglichkeiten

title: Elektroniker (m/w/d)
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Sereact GmbH
description_html:
Wer wir sind

Wir sind ein schnell wachsendes Unternehmen im Bereich Embodied AI, das die menschliche Arbeitswelt revolutioniert. Mit modernster Robotik und fortschrittlicher künstlicher Intelligenz entwickeln wir transformative Technologien, die neu definieren, wie Arbeit über verschiedenste Branchen hinweg erledigt wird — und ermöglichen es Unternehmen, Abläufe zu optimieren, die Produktivität zu steigern und neue Möglichkeiten zu erschließen.

Überblick

Wir suchen einen erfahrenen Elektriker, der die elektrische Verkabelung und Steuerungssysteme unserer autonomen Robotersysteme installiert, verkabelt und in Stand hält. In dieser Rolle arbeitest du eng mit unserem Mechanical- und Hardware-Team zusammen, um sicherzustellen, dass alle elektrischen Komponenten zuverlässig funktionieren und nahtlos in die Gesamtsysteme integriert sind.

Deine Aufgaben

Elektrokonstruktion und Planung:

title: Chief of Staff to the Co-CEO - m/f/d
salary_basis: Based on senior role compensation records at Langdock
description_html:
Help Us Change the Way the World Works

 

Build something that matters.

Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe's largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows - helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.


About the Role

Judith Dada is Co-CEO of Langdock alongside Lennard. She is also Senior Partner at Visionaries Club, serves on the board of Personio, co-founded Relativity Collective, a programme for Europe’s student founders, and writes about AI, creativity, Europe and human flourishing as Dadalogue. She co-authored Europa 2031. What connects all of it is a conviction that technological progress, done well, is how we build a better Europe and a better world.

As Chief of Staff, you will be Judith’s right hand across everything she does. Your job is to extend her reach and impact across Langdock, Europe’s AI ecosystem and beyond. You will structure and execute across a wide surface area, and create the conditions in which Judith does her best work. You will work with her every day, so expect the steepest learning curve of your career.

Langdock’s product is expanding fast in two directions: across the work people do, with chat, agents, meetings, code and apps; and down the stack into our own compute and inference. You will help Judith stay close to the most important work across this growing product surface and the company.

What You Will Do

Run meticulous project management. You will hold the threads across dozens of topics and make sure nothing falls through the cracks. You work half a step ahead, spot bottlenecks before they happen and follow through. You act as an honest broker: synthesising and pressure-testing plans to bring them to their full potential.

Augment Judith’s execution at Langdock. You will keep Judith close to the most important work across a fast-growing product surface. You will prepare her for key decisions, make sure things happen afterwards and support strategic workstreams.

Produce Judith’s ideas. You will structure and challenge Judith’s thinking to draw out the idea worth making, then shape it into a keynote, essay, video, panel, interview or key event. You will help turn customer insights and research into thought leadership that shapes how European leaders think about AI. AI is already an exceptionally capable research assistant; your value lies in depth, taste and operational structure. You do not ghostwrite. You sharpen the thinking and run the flow from first idea to finished piece.

Scale executive engagement. Together with Marketing, you will design exceptional rooms and experiences that bring Europe’s key AI decision-makers together. You will work with our go-to-market teams so Judith’s external work serves the needs of a customer base that is growing quickly.

Extend Judith’s reach into policy and the European AI ecosystem. You will prepare and follow through on policy work and ecosystem initiatives, helping Judith contribute to the conversations shaping AI in Europe.

What Makes This Different

You will work at the forefront of one of the most consequential technological shifts in history. Langdock has grown to around $50M ARR and more than 13,000 customers while remaining profitable and independent of outside investment. You will join at a moment when our product is expanding quickly and Europe needs AI companies built from Europe for the world.

Judith is Co-CEO of Langdock, Senior Partner at Visionaries Club and active across the European AI ecosystem. This role gives you a front-row seat across that breadth of work, with direct responsibility for helping turn ideas and decisions into action.

This is a tour of duty. We ask for a commitment of at least two years, with the explicit prospect of shaping a longer-term role together once we know where you shine. The scope is broad, the feedback loops are short and the learning curve is steep.

You Might Be a Fit If…

  • You have a few years of experience in consulting, investing or a startup that grew quickly. You know how to structure chaos and are still incredibly hungry to learn.

  • You have a deep fascination with technology and AI, and a real belief that technological progress can build a better world.

  • You have impeccable taste. You know what good looks like in a sentence, a slide, an event and an argument, and you can act with confidence in Judith’s stead.

  • You have range and depth. You can switch context many times a day and still go deep when it counts.

  • You write clearly and speak well in the room, in both German and English.

  • You bring calm and good judgement. You know what matters and what can wait, read people well, and hold them accountable with kindness.

  • You see problems and fix them without being asked, and stay persistent until they are done.

  • You are discreet and trustworthy, because you will see everything.

  • You have an exceptional work ethic and are comfortable with a highly demanding role that includes some travel.

The Environment

You will sit with Judith in our Berlin office at Greifswalder Straße 212, where all 65 of us work together in person. Judith has a dedicated Executive Assistant for calendar, travel and admin. You will work closely with them and with Lennard’s Chief of Staff on day-to-day matters.

Breakfast, lunch and dinner are catered in the office. We look after ourselves, and gym membership and coaching resources are part of the standard package. We value Calm Urgency, Ambitious Execution and Caring Ownership. The vibe is calm but intense.


Next steps

We move fast, and most hiring processes finish within two weeks. If this sounds like your kind of work, we would love to hear from you.

title: Legal Counsel - m/f/d
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Langdock
description_html:
Help Us Change the Way the World Works

Build something that matters.

Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe's largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows - helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.

About the Role

At Langdock, legal is part of the product. Some of Europe's largest and most regulated companies use Langdock for work that involves their most sensitive documents and data. Before a single employee logs in, their legal, data protection and security teams need to be convinced. What we promise about data, models and control becomes real in our contracts, our DPA and the way we answer their questions.

This is where you come in. As Legal Counsel, you own your matters end to end: enterprise contracts, data protection, the regulation that applies to an AI company, compliance and employment law for a growing team. Often you will be the person who gets a deal signed.

In our day-to-day work, we want to show what AI can do for legal work and rethink how work itself gets done with it. We treat every business function as an applied AI discipline. You will design new AI powered workflows, experiment with internal automations, and continuously refine how legal operates using our state-of-the-art products.

What You Will Do

Work directly with customers. Negotiate customer agreements from first call to signature, including DPAs, security and AI terms, DORA addenda for financial services.

Solve open questions. Translate new regulations like the AI Act, DORA, NIS2, the Data Act and the sector rules our customers work under into concrete requirements for our product.

Build the future cloud. Shape the contracts behind our data center and new cloud services, from power and hardware to the terms our customers sign.

Keep the company running. Advise internally on employment law, do corporate housekeeping, own our data protection program, and support in keeping our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 compliance current.

Use Langdock constantly. Build and maintain the agents, playbooks and evals behind our self-serve legal tools. As one of Langdock's most demanding users, your feedback goes straight to Product.

Work with kind individuals. We are a small team of highly ambitious people with low egos. We want to have fun and enjoy working together.

What Makes This Different

You are working at the forefront of potentially the biggest technological shift in history. Working at Langdock prepares you for the future of work.

We went from €1M to €50M+ ARR and becoming profitable. No aggressive sales tactics. No unsustainable burn.

You will join early enough to shape how things work, but late enough that we have traction, customers, and a product people love. The hard part is not convincing people AI matters. It is helping them adopt it well. That is a genuinely interesting problem.

You will also learn fast. Our team is small, the scope is large, and the feedback loops are short. People who joined a year ago are now running critical functions. If you are good, you will grow.

You Might Be a Fit If…

  • You are a qualified lawyer with at least two years of experience in-house at a technology company or advising one. You have negotiated SaaS agreements and DPAs with enterprise counterparties.

  • You have built something – an agent, a workflow, a clause library, a script, a template system. You can tell us what changed because of it.

  • You want to understand the technology behind the products you advise on, not just the contracts around them. You are technical enough to know how SaaS products are built: databases, APIs, integrations, basic architecture.

  • You can write and reason clearly and can tell which risks should stop a deal or feature.

  • You are fluent in German and English. German-law employment and contract work makes German necessary; the team and most customer documents are English.

  • You are a kind person who cares about the people around you.

The Environment

We work from our office in Berlin, Greifswalder Strasse 212. Everyone works together in person because the hardest problems get solved faster at a whiteboard than in a Slack thread. Conversations happen faster, problems get solved quicker, and we actually know each other.

We offer lunch & dinner in the office. We run, go to the gym, and take care of ourselves. Health is not separate from work here, it is part of how we work well.

The vibe is calm but intense. No one is yelling or panicking. But everyone is working hard on things that matter.

Compensation

Salaries are transparent and tied to levels, not negotiation. All roles include equity.

We will figure out the right level together based on your experience and scope. Levels are about the work you own, not your title or years of experience. We narrow down the expected salary range early in the process.

Next steps

We move fast. Most processes complete within two weeks. The process includes a case study based on the kind of questions we handle day to day. We care more about how deep you go and how quickly you get there than about which topics you have covered before.

If this sounds like your kind of work, we would like to meet you.

Compensation: €80K – €120K • Offers Equity

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
salary_basis: Based on senior role compensation records at Secfix
description_html:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.

You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This role is for you if:

  • You've managed a real team and made it ship faster. You've hired for it, run the hard conversations, and know what breaks as it grows — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.

  • You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.

  • You have an exceptional IC track record before becoming a manager. You were a senior/principal engineer before you started managing — you didn't skip into management early because coding wasn't working out.

  • You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.

  • You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations about performance.

  • You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.

  • You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."

  • You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.


What we're looking for

Required

  • 8+ years as a software engineer, including 4+ years managing a team of 8+ and hiring for it yourself

  • You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data

  • Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't

  • You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt

  • You're an engineer at heart. You were senior or principal before you managed, and you can still hold your own in a design review, a debugging session, or building a feature

  • You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook

  • Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK

Nice to have

  • You've grown a team to 15+ at a VC-funded startup

  • Managed tech leads or a second manager

  • Previous experience at a fully remote company

Interview process

We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:

  • 30 min — Intro call with our talent team

  • 45 min — Interview with Grigory

  • 45 min — Technical interview

  • 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI

  • 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders

Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.


What Secfix gives you

  • Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather

  • Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)

  • Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here

  • Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better

  • Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access

  • Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays

  • Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage

  • Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands

  • Tech: MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latest

description_html:
Munich-based hybrid with lots of flexibility.
C1 or C2 German language is essential.

At Secfix, we’re at the forefront of automating security compliance in Europe. We help companies get and stay ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, and SOC 2 fast and easy and reduce hundreds of hours of manual work.

Secfix is run by a 100% remote team with hubs in Munich, Berlin and London. We’re a high-performing team looking for passionate, execution-focused, owners to help us automate security and compliance for modern companies and become the European compliance automation leader.

We’ve just raised our $12M Series A and are backed by top VCs, including Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital.

 

About the Role

title: Senior Product Designer

description_html:
Senior Product Designer @ Secfix

Location: Remote (EMEA) · CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

How do you feel about owning a feature from the first customer conversation to the version that's live in production — writing the spec yourself, pairing closely with engineers through the build, and overseeing your design shipped in production exactly the way you designed it? If that sounds like the right shape of the job — designer who owns, not designer who hands off — read on.

I've spent most of my career believing the best designers aren't the ones with the prettiest Figma files. They're the ones who can frame a problem, write a spec, sit with engineers through the build, and own that what shipped is what they designed. Our founding product designer, Ghada, has been doing exactly that since we started. The engineering team has doubled, and we're shipping faster than we ever have. We're hiring the third designer because there's more good work to do than two people can handle — and we'd rather ship faster than slow down.


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to European market leadership.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of product design work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.

What we believe

Compliance software has historically been built like the audit it automates — heavy, defensive, ugly. We're building something else. The customer is a real person trying to ship audit-ready evidence on a Friday afternoon. The product should respect their time, automate the boring parts, and make the rest feel calm.

Quality is the product. Most of our category competes on feature lists. We compete on craft. A clear empty state, a sync that doesn't lie, a settings page that holds together at eleven permission tiers — these are the things customers feel before they can name them. Design at Secfix is not what wraps the product. It's most of what makes it work.

What the role is

We expect strong design skills, strong product thinking, and the ability to hold your own in a technical discussion. You work in a small team — usually with one or two engineers — and pair closely from the first prototype through to production. You own the project from beginning to end.

Alongside the features you ship, you do three things that make everyone else faster:

  • Maintain the components and patterns that make design fast.

  • Own how the team ships. We have no PMs. You write the specs, run the ticketing workflow, keep engineers unblocked.

  • Build the tools and skills — Cursor rules, design QA skills, prompt templates — that let engineers do good design work without you in the room.

The leverage is doing all four well. Doing only one is the wrong shape.

How we work

  • No PMs. Designers and engineers run product. You talk to customers, frame the problem, write the spec, decide what ships.

  • Small temporary teams. You plus one or two engineers per project. Whoever is closest to the problem leads.

  • Design leads the logic; engineering tests feasibility. You bring the V1. Engineers push back on what's expensive or risky, and start ahead with system design. They help spot edge cases. You adjust it fast. We get from v1 to v4 in a matter of hours or a few days.

  • Prototype-grade, not wireframes. Real components, real states, real copy. Sometimes an LLM-built prototype before Figma. The component library stays current because the speed of design depends on it.

  • Handoff is the beginning, not the end. You're in the engineering channel. You review the PR. You verify on production. Staging QA is the first gate, not the last.

  • In-sync culture with a thoughtful comms mindset. Loom for reviews, Notion for specs, quick loops in Gather where written comms don’t cut it, all happening in the same time zone. Teammates are reviewing things quickly. Engineers and designers spend under two hours in weekly meetings.

  • AI is part of the craft. We use Claude to pressure-test ideas, draft specs, surface edge cases, and write test cases. Not to skip thinking.

The first three months

  • Month 1. Ship your first design to production. Get into the codebase, the customer language, the way we write specs. Sit on customer calls.

  • Month 2. Own a full feature end-to-end. Customer conversations, problem framing, Figma, spec, engineer pairing, PR review, production verification.

  • Month 3 and beyond. Push the design system forward. Start building the tools and skills that make engineers faster at design. Improve the product design process. The bar is yours to defend.

Who you are

  • 8+ years designing B2B SaaS desktop applications as Staff/Principal Product Designer or similar. Dense interfaces — tables, filters, permissions, settings pages.

  • You've been the only designer, or one of two or three, in companies under 50 people at least once before. You know how to set the bar without a design org behind you.

  • Your portfolio is "I," not "we." You can name the engineer you paired with on each feature, the design decision you defended through the build, and what happened when the feature reached users.

  • You communicate clearly and concisely in English: in Slack, in docs and on a call.

  • You're fast in Figma with or without AI. You’re already in a serious relationship with LLMs.

  • You treat engineering feasibility as input, not a constraint. When an engineer says "three weeks, here's why," you find the version that's 80% as good and ships next week.

  • You're comfortable doing product work without the PM title.

  • You hear feedback and come back the next day with something better. You don't spend the hour in between defending the version that's already outdated.

Compensation

Salary + equity based on experience. The offered compensation depends on the individual's qualifications assessed during the interview process.

What we offer

  • Generous equity. Everyone is an owner.

  • 26 days holiday + local public holidays.

  • Comprehensive health insurance.

  • €1,000 annual personal development budget.

  • Remote workspace and co-working budget.

  • Latest equipment.

  • Team summits 1-2x per year. Recent ones: Alicante, Costa Brava, Austrian Alps, Milan.

  • Local hubs in Munich, Berlin, London. Visa support if you want to relocate.

Interview process

We aim to invite you to a first conversation within a week and give feedback after every stage.

  • Intro call with talent team (~45 min)

  • Portfolio conversation with product designer (~45 min)

  • Collaborative design task (compensated, a couple of hours over the span of 2-3 days)

  • Final interview with Grigory (~60 min)

Order may flex depending on availability. If you make it to the exercise and don't get an offer, we'll tell you specifically what got in the way.

Learn how we think and work

  • How we designed remote culture at Secfix

  • Thoughtful communication at Secfix

  • Building production-grade product with AI in 2026

  • Building what customers need, not what they ask for

  • Our zero-bug policy

  • Crafting quality that endures — Karri Saarinen's Config talk

We are an equal-opportunity employer and a remote-only company. We hire within EU time zones. We work in sync using Gather as our virtual office and don't support fully asynchronous work.

description_html:
Wemolo runs its commercial engine on Salesforce and RevOps owns it — along with the wider system landscape around it. Our data model is non-standard and our motion is anything but off-the-shelf, so we need an experienced RevOps Systems Manager who can run and improve the whole setup largely on their own, with the Head of RevOps as a soundboard. This is a builder role on a builder team, not a ticket queue, in an environment that leans heavily into AI. You own the platform end-to-end and set the standard for how change happens on it.

What to Expect

  • Ownership: Own Salesforce as our commercial system of record — its health, architecture and evolution across our data model, run and improve the surrounding system landscape (Weflow, Demodesk, Amplemarket and their integrations).

  • Architecture: Drive Salesforce architecture improvements so pipeline data becomes trustworthy.

  • Build: Build no-code / low-code configuration (Flows etc.) customizing and combining tools to solve recurring operational problems.

  • Cross-functional impact: Own changes that span Marketing, BizDev, Sales, CSM, Product and Finance and never deploy one without bringing the affected users along. A change is done when it's adopted, not when it ships.

  • AI-first: Put AI to work in daily admin — drafting validation rules, auditing duplicates, QA — in line with our heavy AI bet.

  • Enablement: Provide technical mentoring to our Junior GTM Engineer and guide the working students on Salesforce and systems topics.

Inspire Us By

  • 3–5+ years as a Salesforce Administrator or RevOps Systems Manager, ideally in a fast-moving commercial/RevOps environment

  • Proven ability to run and improve a CRM and its surrounding tool landscape largely independently — you don't need direction, you need a soundboard

  • Deep no-code / low-code craft: configuration, flows, third-party applications and combining tools/integrations to solve real operational problems

  • A data-quality mindset: You can trace why pipeline data is untrustworthy and fix it at the root

  • Structured, cross-team problem-solving and strong stakeholder communication; you write change announcements and documentation people actually act on

  • An ownership mindset: Builder, not service desk

  • Comfort working AI-first in daily admin

  • Salesforce certifications and experience with other GTM tools

  • English fluency, German is a plus

What we offer

  • Flexibility & Responsibility: Your workday, your performance – Our hybrid model empowers you to focus from home, get fresh perspectives during workation, and connect in person during our Anchor Days (Tuesday to Thursday)

  • Tailored Mobility: Full speed ahead – Whether it’s sustainable bike leasing or a public transport subsidy, we keep you flexible and on the move

  • Ownership & Autonomy: Your impact, your results – Take full ownership of your area and your KPIs

  • Security & Stability: Safe harbor, clear course – Your job with us isn’t a gamble, but set on a steady path. We grow sustainably so you can fully focus on your personal and professional development

  • Team Culture & Networking: Real connections – also beyond the day-to-day. Celebrate successes with us at legendary team events and spirit days

  • Productive Environment: Brainfood deluxe – Whether it's portafilter coffee, Bella&Bona online cafeteria, fresh fruit or our muesli bar – your wellbeing fuels your performance

  • Health & Balance: Stay in balance with EGYM Wellpass or Urban Sports Club – access 1,000+ gyms and wellness spots across Germany

  • Top Equipment & Ergonomics: Mac or Windows, in the office or remote – we make sure you’re set up for efficiency and comfort

Innovation through diversity

Regardless of your background, origin, gender identity, or individual circumstances, it's your personality that interests us. That's why we're committed to building a culture of collaboration and respect, where every team member has a voice, can grow, and feels valued with us.

title: Creative Strategist
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Yepoda
description_html:
About Yepoda

Clean K-Beauty Innovation. No compromises.

Yepoda is a clean K-Beauty brand that actually proves it works. We make Korean skincare without any of the compromises. Everything is clinically tested, 100% vegan, and formulated above EU standards. So you get the innovation and the results that K-Beauty is known for, plus a real commitment to sustainability. And we make it genuinely fun and easy to use — skincare you actually look forward to.

Founded in 2020 by Sander Joonyoung van Bladel and Veronika Strotmann, Yepoda is a certified B Corp™ and 1% for the Planet member, based in the heart of Berlin. Our products are available through our own online shop and, since March 2025, at Sephora Europe — online and in over 650 stores. With a team of 140+ brilliant individuals from around the world, we are actively shaping Yepoda's story every day.

As Creative Strategist, you will sit at the intersection of performance marketing and our creative team, translating data into the stories, hooks, and formats that drive Yepoda's paid social growth. Your focus is to turn day-to-day performance metrics into actionable creative direction, keeping design, content, and influencer teams aligned on what's winning and why, while building the testing roadmaps that keep our creative pipeline ahead of platform trends.

Your Tasks

  • Deliver detailed, actionable creative briefs, direct-response copy, and frame-by-frame storyboards for the design team.

  • Monitor day-to-day micro-metrics (thumb-stop ratios, 3-second hold rates, CTR) to rapidly diagnose asset performance and propose modular iterations.

  • Act as the bridge between performance and creative by streamlining the asset request pipeline and managing the feedback loop between media buyers and designers.

  • Supply the in-house production and influencer teams with data-backed insights, winning hooks, and performance trends to guide their shoots.

  • Proactively design and build A/B testing roadmaps for new hooks, visual formats, and messaging angles.

  • Define and map specific creative concepts and angles to targeted consumer personas for both evergreen (BAU) and seasonal campaigns.

  • Spot native platform trends by maintaining a swipe file of Meta vs. TikTok content and mapping competitor strategies.

  • Present monthly reviews by synthesizing weekly learnings into macro-level creative presentations for stakeholders.

  • Own post-click/CRO alignment by auditing and advising on e-commerce landing pages to ensure the post-click experience matches the ad narrative.

  • Build secondary channel playbooks by adapting winning Meta/TikTok creatives for expansion channels like Pinterest, Snapchat, or Reddit.

Your Profile

  • 4+ years of experience in a creative strategy or content strategy, ideally within a D2C or e-commerce brand and in touch with performance marketing.

  • Proven experience optimizing paid social creative assets for Meta and/or TikTok, with a strong understanding of how platform algorithms use creative signals to define audience targeting.

  • Comfortable working with performance data (thumb-stop ratios, hold rates, CTR) to diagnose what's working and translate it into new creative angles, not just report on it.

  • Experience writing creative briefs, scripts, or storyboards for a design team; visual production skills (e.g. Canva) are a plus but not required.

  • Strong cross-functional collaborator, comfortable aligning performance marketing, design, content, and influencer teams around a shared creative direction.

  • Familiarity with workflow and creative analytics tools (e.g. Motion or similar).

  • Fluent in English; Italian or French language is a plus.

What We Offer

  • Dynamic Environment: The opportunity to work in a start-up environment surrounded by a passionate and dedicated team.

  • Accelerate Your Career: Take on responsibility from day 1, with room for professional growth and advancement as the company continues to expand.

  • Inspiring Workspace: Located in the heart of Berlin's Prenzlauer Berg, a dog-friendly office, with free drinks and snacks.

  • Hybrid Working: We understand that sometimes you get more stuff done from home and need a change of scenery.

  • We Value Diversity: We seek to build an inclusive workplace that welcomes people from all different backgrounds. A welcoming, international, dedicated team with flat hierarchies and trust by default.

  • Employee Discounts: You’ll get to enjoy the Yepoda products at a discount and share it with friends and family to keep your glow going!

  • Unique Add Ons: A monthly benefits budget that's yours to spend. Through the Probonio app you pick what actually fits your lifestyle.

Would you like to be part of the team? Then we'd love to hear from you! 🫰✨

Make sure to apply by clicking on the “Apply for this job” button below. Please upload your CV and Cover Letter in English language. Our Talent Acquisition team will review your application and get back to you as soon as possible.

At Yepoda we are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals, regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, national origin, citizenship, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, parental status, disability, or any other status protected by applicable law.

About the role

We're looking for a Working Student – Product QA Engineer who is curious, detail-oriented, and passionate about building great products. You'll learn how to help us test new features before they reach our users, making sure everything works as expected and delivers a great user experience.

Once trained this will be a hands-on role focused primarily on manual testing. You'll work closely with our Product and Engineering teams, learning how modern software is built while helping us identify bugs, usability issues, and opportunities to improve the product.

If you're someone who naturally spots when something feels "off" and enjoys figuring out why, we'd love to hear from you.


What You'll Do 🎯

  • Test new features across our web and mobile products.

  • Follow test scenarios and explore features from a user's perspective.

  • Identify bugs, inconsistencies, and usability issues.

  • Document your findings clearly so the team can reproduce and fix issues.

  • Work closely with Product Managers and Engineers to verify fixes.

  • Help improve our testing processes as you learn more about the product.

  • Learn about automated testing and support QA initiatives over time.


What You'll Bring 💡

  • You're currently studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field (add any other related degrees).

  • You have a strong attention to detail and enjoy solving problems.

  • You're interested in software quality and creating great user experiences.

  • You're organized, reliable, and comfortable learning new tools.

  • Good communication skills in English.

  • Basic technical knowledge (e.g. how websites or apps work) is a plus.

  • Any experience with testing, coding, or personal software projects is a bonus but not required.

What Makes You a Great Fit 🌟

  • You notice the small details that others often miss.

  • You enjoy thinking like a user and asking, "Does this actually feel right?"

  • You're curious, eager to learn, and not afraid to ask questions.

  • You take ownership of your work and enjoy collaborating with different teams.

  • You like technology and want to understand how products are built.

  • You're excited to gain practical experience in a fast-paced startup environment

  • Other Benefits: Transport subsidy, breakfasts and lunches, language learning, Urban Sports Club, and more.

We believe in fostering talent, evaluating all skill levels during the hiring process, and providing a clear path for growth. Almedia is an equal opportunity employer. We embrace and celebrate diversity, and encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply.

salary_basis: Based on senior role compensation records at Almedia
description_html:
This isn’t your regular job. Almedia is a place where those who want to push harder can accelerate their careers faster than anywhere else. We’re aiming to become Germany’s second bootstrapped unicorn. Almedia is already Europe’s #3 fastest-growing company in 2025 (FT1000).

We are building the future of marketing by rewarding our community of over 80 million users for engaging with our advertisers’ products. We are offering a new way to acquire users for the biggest companies in the world.

Product Manager

€70K – €100K | Offers Equity

At Almedia, you’ll:

  • Own way more, way earlier — you’ll be trusted with responsibility fast.

  • Push harder, get further — this isn’t a 9–5. We highly reward intensity.

  • Join a rare environment — you will work with ambitious high-speed, high-ownership people.

  • Fully present — we’re 5 days a week in the office to build the energising momentum we need.

Freecash is the product. Almedia is the engagement engine behind it: the smartest way for mobile game studios to turn high-potential users into high-value ones. We're the leader in our category, profitable, and now expanding into new verticals to capture a much bigger market.

We're hiring a Product Manager to join the team and own real outcomes. You won't be running the whole roadmap on day one. You'll own the results of the projects you take on, have a real say in where the roadmap goes, and take on as much as you can carry. The more you can own, the more we'll hand you.

If you think like a founder, get energy from hard problems, and want to dig into data and turn it into something worth building, keep reading.

What you'll own

You won't be handed a list of tickets. You'll be handed problems and trusted to solve them.

  • The outcomes of your projects, not just the tasks. You own the result of the work you take on, from the problem all the way to shipped impact to millions of daily active users.

  • A real say in the roadmap. You bring ideas, push back, and heavily influence what we build and why.

  • Room to make the call. You'll own your decisions without waiting for sign-off on everything. We back conviction, and a bet that doesn't land is a lesson, not a mark against you.

  • As much ownership as you can carry. We hand more to the people who prove they can run with it. Show us, and your scope grows fast.

What you'll bring

  • You think like a founder. You operate like an owner: figuring out what matters, making the call with incomplete information, and getting it done without waiting to be told.

  • You live in the data. You don't ask the analyst what the chart says. You dig in yourself, follow the thread, and come back with the insight nobody else found. Hungry to get hands-on with tools like Amplitude, Hex, and Looker.

  • You go deep and think wide. Data tells you what to solve. Creativity decides how. You explore a few ways to crack a problem before committing, because the obvious answer is rarely the best one.

  • You prioritize and you ship. You pick the few things that matter right now and drive them from idea to launch. Strong bias for action.

  • You communicate and align. You bring developers, data, design, and business development with you without slowing down.

  • Impact. We don't count years in a PM title. If you spent two years building your own company and one year in product, that counts. We care about what you've built and the impact you've had.

What puts you ahead

These aren't requirements, but they're the patterns we keep seeing in people who thrive here.

  • You founded a company, and now you want to go all-in on product. This is golden to us. You know what it means to own an outcome with no one to hand it off to, and you'd rather pour that energy into building product than into anything else right now.

  • You've worked in a fast-moving startup. Bonus if you were there through real growth. Shifting priorities and building the plane mid-flight feel normal to you.

  • You want to grow fast. You're here to do the best work of your career so far, and you'll take on everything you can handle to get there.

Why Almedia? 🚀

  • Own Our Growth: We offer all Berlin-based employees equity in Almedia to truly be a part of our success.

  • Scale With Almedia: Grow alongside a startup that has been profitable from day one.

  • Central Berlin Office: Work from a fully-stocked modern office built for collaboration, accessible from all around Berlin.

  • Other Benefits: Transport subsidy, breakfasts and lunches, language learning, Urban Sports Club, and more.

We believe in fostering talent, evaluating all skill levels during the hiring process, and providing a clear path for growth. Almedia is an equal opportunity employer. We embrace and celebrate diversity, and encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply.

Compensation: €70K – €100K • Offers Equity

title: Full-Stack Engineer - Team Decide
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Taktile
description_html:
About the Role

Taktile enables financial institutions to transform into AI-native organizations that are increasingly powered by autonomous agents.

With our modular Agentic Decision Platform, customers combine AI agents, rules, relevant context, and human oversight to safely automate and optimize their decisions—approving more customers, reimbursing claims instantly, stopping fraud before it spreads, and financing every business worth funding.

Founded in 2020, Taktile powers millions of decisions daily for institutions including Mercury, Allianz, Faire, and Pleo. With offices in New York, Berlin, London, São Paulo, and Iași, the company has raised $184M from Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Index Ventures, Tiger Global, Balderton Capital, and Y Combinator. Learn more at taktile.com.

We're looking for a Full-stack Engineer to join our engineering team. In Team Decide you'll focus on designing the distributed execution engine that runs customer workflows. You'll own critical systems end-to-end on a team where your decisions shape the product.

What You'll Do

  • Build and operate backend services in Python on AWS — Lambda functions, DynamoDB, Aurora, and event-driven pipelines that handle real production traffic. You'll leverage agentic AI tools as part of your daily workflow.

  • Work on exciting AI initiatives such as MCP servers, agentic co-pilot

  • Tackle hard backend problems — latency, reliability, and scalability are everyday concerns.

  • Contribute to systems end-to-end, from implementation and testing to deployment and monitoring

  • Contribute to technical and architectural decisions, working with the team to evaluate trade-offs.

  • Contribute to code reviews and help improve our development tooling and processes.

  • Work directly with Product and Design to shape what we build next.

Requirements

  • At least 3 years of professional full-stack software engineering experience, with experience delivering moderately complex projects or features.

  • Experience in React

  • Experience working with Design Systems to ensure a consistent UX among different parts of the product.

  • Good communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • The ability to work in a hybrid model from our Berlin HQ, the London office, or the Iasi hub. Please note that relocation assistance is not provided for this role.

Ideal, But Not Required

  • Familiarity with system design concepts and architectural trade-offs

  • AWS Serverless experience at scale (Lambda, SAM, CloudFormation, DynamoDB, Aurora…)

Our Offer

  • Work with colleagues that lift you up, challenge you, celebrate you and help you grow. We come from many different backgrounds, but what we have in common is the desire to operate at the very top of our fields. If you are similarly capable, caring, and driven, you'll find yourself at home here.

  • Experience a truly flat hierarchy and communicate directly with founding team members. Having an opinion and voicing your ideas is not only welcome but encouraged, especially when they challenge the status quo.

  • Learn from experienced mentors and achieve tremendous personal and professional growth. Get to know and leverage our network of leading tech investors and advisors around the globe.

  • Receive a top-of-market equity and cash compensation package.

  • Get access to a self-development budget you can use to e.g. attend conferences, buy books or take classes.

  • Receive a new Apple MacBook Pro, as well as meaningful home office set-up.

 

Our Stance

  • We're eager to meet talented and driven candidates regardless of whether they tick all the boxes. We're looking for someone who will add to our culture, not just fit within it. We strongly encourage individuals from groups traditionally underestimated and underrepresented in tech to apply.

  • We seek to actively recognize and combat racism, sexism, ableism and ageism. We embrace and support all gender identities and expressions, and celebrate love in its many forms. We won't inquire about how you identify or if you've experienced discrimination, but if you want to tell your story, we are all ears.

 

About Us

Taktile enables financial institutions to transform into AI-native organizations that are increasingly powered by autonomous agents.

With our modular Agentic Decision Platform, customers combine AI agents, rules, relevant context, and human oversight to safely automate and optimize their decisions—approving more customers, reimbursing claims instantly, stopping fraud before it spreads, and financing every business worth funding.

Founded in 2020, Taktile powers millions of decisions daily for institutions including Mercury, Monzo, Faire, and Pleo.

With offices in New York, Berlin, London, São Paulo, and Iași, the company has raised $184M from Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Index Ventures, Tiger Global, Balderton Capital, and Y Combinator. Learn more at taktile.com.

 

About Your Employment. Taktile operates through regional entities worldwide. Depending on the location of this role, your employment or engagement will be with Taktile LLC (US), Taktile GmbH (Germany), Taktile Ltd (UK), or Taktile SRL (Romania). The applicable entity will be confirmed during the offer process.

Your Privacy. Taktile (“we” or “us”) is the controller of the personal data you provide during this application process. We collect and process your name, contact details, resume/CV, work history, education, and any other information you submit or that we obtain from publicly available sources or references.

How we use your data: We process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy, communicate with you about the recruitment process, comply with legal obligations (such as right-to-work verification), and, with your consent, to consider you for future opportunities.

Legal basis (EU/UK applicants): We rely on (i) pre-contractual steps at your request (GDPR/UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)), (ii) legal obligations (Art. 6(1)(c)), and (iii) our legitimate interest in evaluating candidates (Art. 6(1)(f)).

Retention: If your application is unsuccessful, we retain your data for 12 months after the recruitment process concludes, unless you consent to longer retention. Successful candidates’ data becomes part of their employment records.

Your rights: Depending on your location, you may have the right to access, correct, delete, or restrict the processing of your personal data, to data portability, and to withdraw consent.

Automated decision-making: We use automated tools to assist in screening applications. No hiring decision is made solely by automated means without human review.

International transfers: Your data may be transferred to and processed in the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, or Romania. Where required, transfers are protected by Standard Contractual Clauses or other approved mechanisms.
